Summary: Dynamic creation of a Read DER Control List child exchange for every DERProgram href returned in a DER Program List response, named with the client and end device IDs.
Preconditions:
Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to an IEEE 2030.5 server exposing at least 2 DERProgram resources under a DERProgramList.
Under the DERProgram has DER Controls configured as well.
Actions:
1. File -> Select Protocol -> IEEE 2030.5
2. Configure/Enable "Read DER Program List" exchange and send the exchange.
3. Allow exchange to poll/respond
4. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: 1. For each DERProgram href returned in the DERProgramList response, an appropriate "Read DER Control List" exchange is dynamically created and appended to the Exchange List. Name format: <TemplateBaseName>_Client <ClientID>_<EndDeviceID>

Summary: Dynamic creation of a Read DER Control List child exchange from the DERControlList link in a DER Program response.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a discovered DER Program exchange whose response contains a DERControlList link.
Actions:
1. Allow "Read DER Program" exchange to receive a response.
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: 1. One "Read DER Control List" child exchange are dynamically created from the same parent DER Program response

Summary: Dynamic creation of one Execute DER Control child exchange per DERControl href found in a DER Control List response.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a discovered DER Control List exchange whose response contains one or more DERControl hrefs
Actions:
1. Allow "Read DER Control List" (dynamically created) exchange to receive a response.
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: 1. One "Execute DER Control" child exchange is dynamically created per DERControl href found in the list

Summary: Object data layout of a dynamically created exchange matches that of its static template exchange; only the href and response values differ.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a statically-configured "Read DER Program"/"Read DER Control"/"Read Default DER Control Settings" template exchange present in Protocol.xml
Actions:
1. Trigger discovery so a dynamic child of each type is spawned.
2. Double-click OR Right-click -> Exchange Properties on the dynamically-created exchange
Expected Results: 1. The Application Layer Object Data structure (0:GET, response object) of the dynamically-created exchange is identical in layout to its corresponding static template exchange, only the request URL (href) and populated response values differ

Summary: Values already parsed from the parent response (mRID, description, links, hrefs) are pre-populated in the child exchange instead of placeholder "*" values.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a DER Program List response already parsed for a specific DERProgram entry
Actions:
1. Allow dynamic "Read DER Program" child exchange to be created for that entry
2. Exchange Properties -> Object Properties on the response object
Expected Results: 1. Field values already known from the parent's parsed sub-tree (mRID, description, links, href attributes) are pre-populated in the new child exchange's response object rather than left as placeholder "*" values

Summary: Re-polling or re-parsing a parent response containing an already discovered href does not create additional exchanges.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a dynamic child exchange already created for a given href
Actions: 1. Re-poll or re-parse the same parent response containing the same href
Expected Results: 1. No additional exchange is created for that href; exchange count for the AP function remains unchanged

Summary: Names of dynamically created exchanges carry the correct ClientID and EndDevice ID scope when several clients or end devices are connected.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to multiple Clients and/or End Devices, each exposing DER resources
Actions:
1. Trigger discovery across multiple clients/end devices.
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: 1. Each dynamically-created exchange name follows the format <BaseName> <Index>_Client <ClientID>[_EndDevice <EndDevID>], correctly scoped to the client/end device that produced it (not shared across clients/devices)

Summary: Exchanges are created hierarchically from End Device through FSA, DER List, DER Program List, DER Control List and DER Control during discovery.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to a server exposing an EndDeviceList
Actions:
1. Enable "Read End Device List" exchange.
2. Allow discovery to proceed through End Device -> FSA List/DER List -> DER Program List chain.
3. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: 1. Exchanges are dynamically created in sequence: Read FunctionSet Assignments List and Read DER List (per End Device) and Read DER Program List (per FSA), and Read DER Control List (per Program List), and finally Read DER Control reflecting the discovered resource hierarchy

Summary: Hierarchical dynamic exchange creation when the config generator Index and Comm files are imported and transmit is enabled with the play button.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to a server.
Actions:
1. Import the Index file for configured end devices created from config generator.
2. Import the Comm file for config generator.
3. Hit the play button.
Expected Results: 1. Exchanges are dynamically created in sequence: Read FunctionSet Assignments List and Read DER List (per End Device) and Read DER Program List (per FSA), and Read DER Control List (per Program List), and finally Read DER Control reflecting the discovered resource hierarchy after importing index file generated using config generator.

Summary: GET request built from a static Read FunctionSet Assignment exchange with a bound href: request line, empty body and host/port from the channel configuration.
Preconditions: ASE2000 configured as IEEE 2030.5 client in Exchange Mode; "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange present with DLControl = GET and Object[0] href set to a valid DER Control resource URL (not */blank)
Actions:
1. File > Select Protocol > IEEE 2030.5
2. Configure "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange and trigger a Play/Send on the exchange.
3. Capture outgoing HTTP request
Expected Results: 1. Request line is GET <href> HTTP/1.1 with no body; Content-Length/body absent; correct Host/port used from channel config.

2. Configure "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange and trigger a Play/Send on the exchange.
3. Capture incoming HTTP response
Expected Results: 1. Proper response with necessary details is received and displayed in the line monitor.

3. Inspect exchange Object properties values after response.
Expected Results: 1. All expected fields are populated in the exchange's object data and visible in Property Grid; values match response XML exactly.

Summary: The pollRate attribute in a server response updates the transmission frequency of the exchange.
Preconditions: Response contains a pollRate attribute (or exchange Object data has pollRate-tagged attribute)
Actions:
1. Server returns response including pollRate="X".
2. Observe exchange's configured frequency after processing.
Expected Results: 1. IEEE2030_5Ex->PollRate updated to X;

Summary: opModConnect in a scheduled DERControl is accepted and executed when Execute DER Control is sent manually, with an acknowledgement POSTed to the replyTo URI.

Actions:
1. Send the Execute DER Control of a particular end device.
2. View Messages/Line Monitor.
Expected Results: 1. Execution proceeds and an acknowledgement POST request is supplied to the appropriate replyTo URI.

Expected Results: 1. A WARN log message is generated identifying the unsupported operation mode and the associated exchange href;

Summary: A 200 OK response to an acknowledgement PUT/POST is correlated to the originating exchange by CopyCommandVal2Status().

Expected Results: 1. The 200 OK response is correlated back to the originating exchange via CopyCommandVal2Status(); exchange status reflects successful acknowledgement

2. Allow execution logic to run on a discovered control
Expected Results: 1. Dynamic child exchange creation, naming, and hierarchy behave as previously validated; execution logic does not interfere with discovery/creation of new DER Control exchanges

3. Open Exchange Tree.
Expected Results: 1. DERProgramList, DERProgram, DERControlList, DERControl and DefaultDERControl exchanges are created.

Summary: Five new DER exchanges are appended to the IEEE 2030.5 Exchange List with default Flags, Freq, ClientID, EndDev ID and ServerID values.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode
Actions:
1. File -> Select Protocol -> IEEE 2030.5
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results:
The following 5 exchange must be there at the end of the list:
1. Read DER Program List
2. Read DER Program
3. Read DER Control List
4. Read DER Control
5. Read Default DER Control Settings
By default,
Flags must be set to Display,
Freq to 2.00,
ClientID to *,
EndDev ID to *,
ServerID to *

Summary: Exchange Properties common to the five new exchanges: name, frequency, channel, flags, IEEE 2030.5 properties, application layer functions and object data items.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode
Actions:
1. File -> Select Protocol -> IEEE 2030.5
2. View -> Exchange List
For all 5 new exchanges:
3. Double-click OR Right-click -> Exchange Properties
Expected Results:
The following must be common across all 5 new exchanges:
1. Name
2. Frequency (Secs.)
3. Channel (Disabled)
Flags:
1. Display
2. Event
3. Transmit
IEEE 2030.5 Specific Properties:
1. ClientID
2. EndDev ID
3. ServerID
Application Layer:
A. Function
This dropdown must now also contain:
16: RDERPROGLST
17: RDERPROG
18: RDERCTRLLST
19: RDERCTRL
20: RDEFDERCTRL
B. The following Object Data items:
0: GET | 0:Request
<A second Object Data item specific to that exchange> | 1:Response
